identity.title: Mean Flows for One-step Generative Modeling

problem.claim: Develop a principled framework for one-step generative modeling.

gap.claim: The study targets the remaining performance gap between one-step diffusion/flow models and their multi-step predecessors.

contributions.claim: Introduces average velocity as a flow-field concept distinct from the instantaneous velocity modeled by Flow Matching.
Derives an identity relating average and instantaneous velocities and uses it to guide neural-network training.
Presents MeanFlow, a self-contained model requiring no pre-training, distillation, or curriculum learning.

stated_novelty.claim: The stated new distinction is to characterize flow fields through average rather than instantaneous velocity, with a derived identity connecting the two for training.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report an FID of 3.43 at 1-NFE on ImageNet 256×256, trained from scratch.
The authors report that MeanFlow significantly outperforms previous state-of-the-art one-step diffusion/flow models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Proposes a principled framework for one-step generative modeling.
Defines average velocity in contrast to Flow Matching’s instantaneous velocity.
Derives an average–instantaneous velocity identity and applies it to neural-network training.
Names the resulting self-contained, from-scratch MeanFlow model and lists its lack of pre-training, distillation, and curriculum requirements.
Reports strong ImageNet one-step performance and a narrowed gap to multi-step predecessors.

source_observation.claim: The abstract introduces a modeling distinction, makes the relationship to an existing quantity explicit, and uses the resulting identity to guide training.

lessons.interpretation: A precise conceptual bridge can make a method’s training rationale easier to state and evaluate.
lessons.application: When proposing a new parameterization, define it against the closest existing quantity and state the exact relationship that determines the training signal.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when no meaningful correspondence exists or when the relationship cannot be specified without substantial omitted assumptions.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the derivation, architecture, training objective, dataset protocol, or baseline details behind the reported FID and comparison.
The claimed significance of the performance comparison is author-reported; statistical procedures and reproduced results are not provided.
